Definitions.Title: Incomplete service-principal evidence collection
Definitions.Rationale: Unavailable evidence must remain distinguishable from a confirmed empty result so absence-based conclusions are not overstated.
Definitions.Recommendation: Resolve the reported collection failure and rerun the affected identity before treating absence-based conclusions as authoritative.

Definitions.Title: Incomplete application-registration evidence collection
Definitions.Rationale: Application ownership and credential evidence is first-class assessment data and remains distinct from the linked service-principal relationship.
Definitions.Recommendation: Resolve the reported collection failure and rerun before treating owner or credential conclusions as authoritative.

Definitions.Title: Sensitive application permissions present
Definitions.Rationale: Application permissions operate without a signed-in user and represent standing application identity access.
Definitions.Recommendation: Confirm each app-only grant is required for the workload and remove grants that are no longer justified.

Definitions.Title: Sensitive tenant-wide delegated permissions present
Definitions.Rationale: Tenant-wide delegated consent increases the user population for which the application can exercise the granted permissions.
Definitions.Recommendation: Validate the business need and tenant-wide consent scope; reduce or remove delegated grants that are no longer required.

Definitions.Title: Sensitive user-scoped delegated permissions present
Definitions.Rationale: Delegated grants allow an application to act with a signed-in user context and should remain limited to justified permissions.
Definitions.Recommendation: Validate the business need for each delegated grant and remove grants that are no longer required.

Definitions.Title: Service principal has no owner
Definitions.Rationale: Without an accountable owner, permission and lifecycle review can be delayed or missed.
Definitions.Recommendation: Assign accountable current owners and include the enterprise application in normal ownership review.

Definitions.Title: Service principal has only one owner
Definitions.Rationale: Microsoft recommends proactively monitoring applications to ensure at least two owners where possible, reducing dependency on one individual.
Definitions.Recommendation: Where operationally appropriate, assign a second accountable owner.

Definitions.Title: Disabled account owns service principal
Definitions.Rationale: A disabled account cannot provide reliable ongoing accountability for the enterprise application.
Definitions.Recommendation: Replace disabled owners with active accountable owners.

Definitions.Title: Guest account owns service principal
Definitions.Rationale: Guest ownership can complicate accountability when the external relationship changes.
Definitions.Recommendation: Confirm guest ownership is intentional and retain appropriate tenant-local accountable ownership.

Definitions.Title: Application registration has no owner
Definitions.Rationale: Application-registration ownership is independent from service-principal ownership and provides accountability for registration configuration and credentials.
Definitions.Recommendation: Assign accountable current owners to the application registration.

Definitions.Title: Application registration has only one owner
Definitions.Rationale: Microsoft recommends at least two application owners where possible to reduce dependency on one individual.
Definitions.Recommendation: Where operationally appropriate, assign a second accountable owner to the registration.

Definitions.Title: Disabled account owns application registration
Definitions.Rationale: A disabled account cannot provide reliable ongoing accountability for registration configuration and credentials.
Definitions.Recommendation: Replace disabled owners with active accountable owners.

Definitions.Title: Guest account owns application registration
Definitions.Rationale: Guest ownership can complicate accountability when the external relationship changes.
Definitions.Recommendation: Confirm guest ownership is intentional and retain appropriate tenant-local accountable ownership.

Definitions.Title: Expired application credential remains configured
Definitions.Rationale: Expired credentials create avoidable credential inventory and can indicate incomplete rotation or lifecycle cleanup.
Definitions.Recommendation: Remove expired credentials after confirming they are no longer required.

Definitions.Title: Application credential approaches expiry
Definitions.Rationale: Unplanned credential expiry can interrupt application authentication.
Definitions.Recommendation: Confirm rotation ownership and replace the credential before expiry if it remains required.

Definitions.Title: Long-lived application credential
Definitions.Rationale: Long credential lifetimes increase the period during which compromised credential material can remain usable.
Definitions.Recommendation: Use the shortest practical credential lifetime and rotate long-lived credentials according to organizational policy.

Definitions.Title: Application registration has credential sprawl
Definitions.Rationale: A larger set of simultaneously active credentials increases lifecycle and rotation complexity and can leave obsolete credentials behind.
Definitions.Recommendation: Confirm each active credential is required and remove obsolete credentials after safe rotation validation.

Definitions.Title: Orphan application registration retains active credentials
Definitions.Rationale: Credential material remains configured even though no local service principal is correlated to the registration.
Definitions.Recommendation: Confirm the registration and its credentials are still required; remove obsolete credentials or the registration when appropriate.

Definitions.Title: Disabled service principal retains sensitive permissions
Definitions.Rationale: Disabled state reduces immediate sign-in use but retained sensitive grants remain part of the identity configuration and become effective again if the identity is re-enabled.
Definitions.Recommendation: Confirm retained grants are intentionally preserved and remove unnecessary permissions when the identity is retired.

Definitions.Title: Disabled service principal is linked to active application credentials
Definitions.Rationale: A disabled enterprise application can still be linked to registration credentials that require independent lifecycle management.
Definitions.Recommendation: Confirm the application registration and active credentials are intentionally retained.

Definitions.Title: Inactive application identity review candidate
Definitions.Rationale: No sign-in observed over a sufficiently long review window can help identify application identities that warrant lifecycle review. Microsoft-managed apps, managed identities, and newly created identities are excluded to reduce false positives; absence of observed sign-in still does not prove global inactivity.
Definitions.Recommendation: Confirm the application's business function and expected usage cadence with its owner before removing permissions, credentials, or the identity.

Definitions.Title: Sensitive permissions combined with long-lived credentials
Definitions.Rationale: A long-lived credential linked to a highly privileged application identity increases persistence if credential material is exposed.
Definitions.Recommendation: Review permission necessity and shorten or rotate long-lived credentials as one coordinated remediation.

Definitions.Title: Sensitive permissions without accountable service-principal ownership
Definitions.Rationale: Sensitive standing access without an accountable enterprise-application owner weakens governance around permission review and lifecycle decisions.
Definitions.Recommendation: Assign accountable owners and review the sensitive grants for continued necessity.

Definitions.Title: Sensitive permissions depend on a single service-principal owner
Definitions.Rationale: A privileged application with one owner concentrates governance responsibility in one individual.
Definitions.Recommendation: Where possible, assign a second accountable owner and review the sensitive grants.

Definitions.Title: Sensitive permissions on an inactive review candidate
Definitions.Rationale: Standing sensitive access on an application identity with no observed sign-in over the configured review window is a useful prioritization signal, but the activity evidence is not proof that the application is unused.
Definitions.Recommendation: Validate business use with the accountable owner, then reduce unnecessary permissions or retire the identity only after confirming that the workload is no longer required.

Definitions.Title: Unverified third-party application has sensitive permissions
Definitions.Rationale: Sensitive permissions granted to a third-party application without verified publisher metadata warrant additional trust and business-need validation.
Definitions.Recommendation: Validate the publisher, application provenance, business owner, and necessity of each sensitive grant.

Definitions.Title: Ownerless application registration retains active credentials
Definitions.Rationale: Active credential material without an accountable registration owner combines authentication exposure with weak lifecycle accountability.
Definitions.Recommendation: Assign accountable owners and review whether each active credential remains necessary.

Definitions.Title: Sensitive permissions linked to weak application-registration ownership
Definitions.Rationale: Sensitive service-principal grants rely on an application registration whose ownership is absent or limited to one accountable owner.
Definitions.Recommendation: Strengthen registration ownership and review sensitive grants together as one application identity lifecycle decision.

Definitions.Title: Application registration contains a non-HTTPS browser redirect URI
Definitions.Rationale: Browser redirect URIs are part of the OAuth authorization boundary. Non-HTTPS browser redirects outside loopback development scenarios can expose authorization responses to interception or unintended handlers.
Definitions.Recommendation: Replace non-HTTPS web or SPA redirect URIs with HTTPS endpoints. Retain HTTP only for explicit localhost development scenarios where supported.

Definitions.Title: OAuth implicit token issuance is enabled
Definitions.Rationale: Implicit access-token or ID-token issuance is a legacy browser authentication pattern. Modern applications should normally use authorization code flow with PKCE where applicable.
Definitions.Recommendation: Confirm the application still requires implicit issuance and migrate supported clients to authorization code flow with PKCE before disabling it.

Definitions.Title: Fallback public-client behavior is enabled
Definitions.Rationale: Fallback public-client configuration changes how Microsoft Entra interprets client type when it cannot otherwise determine whether the application is public or confidential.
Definitions.Recommendation: Confirm fallback public-client behavior is intentional for the application's authentication design and disable it when it is not required.

Definitions.Title: Application exposes pre-authorized client access
Definitions.Rationale: Pre-authorized client applications can access specified delegated scopes without an additional user consent prompt, creating an explicit trust relationship that should remain intentional and current.
Definitions.Recommendation: Review each pre-authorized client and delegated permission ID, remove stale relationships, and confirm the trust still matches the application architecture.
